runs.t: Onion Architecture places the domain model at the center and surrounding application, infrastructure, and delivery concerns in concentric layers. The core remains independent of outside technical choices.

Inner domain types express business invariants and contracts; outer rings implement repositories, events, HTTP and integration details. Compile-time dependencies should not flow from the domain into infrastructure; runtime calls may pass through injected interfaces.
A loyalty-points domain applies earn and redeem rules without referencing an ORM. The outer application ring coordinates a transaction; a storage adapter maps records to domain entities.

The onion metaphor does not prescribe a universal folder structure. Avoid ceremonial layers when the domain contains little actual policy; decide how to handle cross-cutting concerns such as logging and transactions.
